rubrics_metrics.name: Tension between irony and sincerity
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal irony should be balanced by genuine moral or emotional seriousness; this productive tension is a craft marker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too much irony without seriousness produces cynicism; too much earnestness without formal self-awareness can feel naive. Skilled maximalist work navigates the balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Development
rubrics_metrics.description: The depth, dimensionality, and authenticity of characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge how well characters grow, change, or persist and whether they are recognizable as human (or as the kind of being they are). Consider complexity, emotional truth, and the role characters play in conveying theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ending feels arrived at, not stopped
rubrics_metrics.description: Endings should feel earned and inevitable given the story's spine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective ending resolves or reframes the dramatic question and stems naturally from character choices and narrative momentum. Avoid tacked-on conclusions, unresolved abruptness, or endings that rely on deus ex machina.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustain a high degree of narrative tension from start to finish
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain escalating stakes and continuous narrative pressure throughout the book so readers stay urgently invested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From summary: 'sustain a high degree of narrative tension from start to finish.' TOC emphasis: 'Stakes', 'Escalating Stakes', 'Tension on Every Page', 'What is the Worst That Can Happen?', 'High Moments, Turning Corners, Killing Characters'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Structure (Narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits a well-structured plot, including a strong beginning, development, and satisfying conclusion (Excellent: "well-structured plot... strong beginning, development, and satisfying conclusion"; lower tiers lack development or coherent conclusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric emphasizes exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, and resolution. Lessons: plot development exercises, use of story maps or prompts, and drafting sequences to ensure clear beginning/middle/end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tension
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatic interest and conflict that sustain reader engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in 'Writer-ly Criteria' as a key dimension; look for elements that create stakes, conflict, or suspense that propel the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition to challenge assumptions and biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Our books embrace writers and audiences who fearlessly shake up our assumptions and biases; and who believe in the power of storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for work that provocatively challenges conventional viewpoints, prompts reflection, or unsettles readers' preconceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metaphor and Figures of Speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Skillful metaphor and figures are essential to striking expression and to revealing truth poetically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective metaphors illuminate and fuse image with idea; avoid mixed or strained figures. Figures should be natural to the thought and strengthen precision and vividness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong, distinct characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters with vivid personalities and clear motivations that drive the story and invite reader identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Jack is a rule-proof bundle of bunny-eared id"; portray characters through actions, voice, and relationships so they feel alive and memorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create Emotional Resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft an ending that leaves readers feeling something—joy, sadness, shock, reflection—by focusing on the characters' emotional journey and how they've changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the emotional payoff to the journey the reader has taken; deliver catharsis when the story builds toward it, or choose a quiet, understated ending for subtle impact. Emotional depth doesn't require melodrama; a restrained ending can be powerful if it reflects honest internal growth or loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public-domain material to leverage shared narrative knowledge and create effective twists
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing builds on shared understanding; twists play off audience expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because readers share cultural touchstones, you can craft efficient pitches and surprising twists by subverting expectations tied to well-known public-domain material (example: 'this, but 20 years later and with this twist'). This is a creative strategy rather than a legal rule, but it's an explicit recommendation of value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose quality at sentence level
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity, rhythm, and sentence-level infelicities: is the writing clear, economical, and effective?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out unclear sentences, awkward diction, tonal inconsistencies, and rhythmic problems. Examples or brief rewrites can illustrate suggestions. Avoid turning the critique into copyediting-only; connect sentence-level notes to larger story goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speeches on the writer's themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters delivering long speeches that mouth the author's themes rather than arising from character or situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let themes emerge from action and conflict; avoid using dialogue as a soapbox for authorial views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent narrative method and point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: The predominant point of view should be coherent. Tolstoy alternates between telling the story himself (authorial narration) and letting characters’ consciousnesses carry the effect; the inconsistency produces different principles governing parts of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose and sustain a narrative method (e.g., free indirect discourse centered on characters, or an authorial narrator) unless shifts are motivated and patterned. Anti-patterns include choosing an onlooker 'at random' or switching viewpoint without a principled reason—such shifts break the unity of effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vividness of imagined setting / worldbuilding
rubrics_metrics.description: The imagined setting should be vividly realised — the time lives, breathes, speaks — with accommodating details of an unfamiliar society that sweep the reader along.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics praise Herbert for the vividness of Arrakis and its ecology; Carl Sagan noted stories that are 'so tautly constructed, so rich in the accommodating details of an unfamiliar society that they sweep me along.' Positive signals include detailed ecology, believable social structures, and sensory detail. Anti-patterns: thin, patchwork or implausible settings that fail to convey a lived-in world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show, don't tell
rubrics_metrics.description: Never force words into a character's mouth to tell the audience about world, history, or person. Instead, dramatize exposition—show honest, natural scenes where characters talk and behave truthfully while indirectly passing along necessary facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let camera or narration simply 'tell' a chain of facts (e.g., panning photographs). 'Show, don't tell' also means characters and camera must behave truthfully; avoid turning film into a home movie or illustrated audio book.

rubrics_metrics.name: comedic_exaggeration_and_ironic_tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Use hyperbole, ironic contrast, and wry observation for humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lines like 'I was the center of breathless attention' or counting 'ninety-nine automobiles and one car' employ comic exaggeration. Irony appears when grand claims (automobiles mean freedom) are juxtaposed with petty town behavior (trading autos in front of the depot). Maintain a lightly mocking narrator to produce humor without malice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climactic scene rushed
rubrics_metrics.description: Rushing the climax so it lacks emotional payoff or clear resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand climactic scenes into full scenes with sensory detail and stakes rather than summarizing them; ensure proper buildup beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative perspective and who the story centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the novel centers the appropriate viewpoint and how that affects reader sympathy; critics argued the book's construction 'makes it easier for sheltered, white American readers to sympathize with the plot.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whose perspectives are prioritized and whether that centering simplifies or reshapes the real dynamics of the subject. A critique can be that an outsider-oriented perspective domesticates complex social realities for outside readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Drive — Escalating Stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each scene should raise what is at risk; stakes should escalate across the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the cost of failure larger or more personal over time so tension increases; avoid scenes where stakes are flat or irrelevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures of Thought and Speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Skillful, effective use of rhetorical devices — metaphor, hyperbole, asyndeton, polysyndeton, apostrophe — deployed to amplify, not decorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rhetorical figures to intensify and clarify thought rather than ornament it; examples include metaphor and apostrophe. Balance and purpose are essential; devices should serve the idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality vs hackneyed imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the depiction uses fresh, thoughtful symbolism or relies on 'vulgar' and frequently repeated clichés.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text criticizes 'vulgar and most frequent conception' and 'grievously hackneyed and vulgarized' images; award originality and condemn cliché (e.g., Spenser's more noble renderings are preferred to common pictorial conventions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance and hierarchy of narrative modes
rubrics_metrics.description: A novelist must understand and deploy the relative uses and values of scene, picture, panorama, generalized narrative, and consciousness-centered report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide which mode suits each portion of the story (scene for climaxes, picture for survey, panoramic for breadth, consciousness for intimacy). The craft requires a working theory of how these modes interrelate and where each is properly used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversals and discoveries (mechanisms of emotion)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Two of the most important elements in the emotional effect of tragedy, 'reversals' and 'discoveries,' are parts of the plot."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include well-constructed reversals (peripeteia) and recognitions (anagnorisis) within the plot to produce effective pity and fear. These are chief tools for achieving catharsis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery must be coherent and imaginable
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism of images that cannot be realized imaginatively (e.g. a man’s heart leaning toward the stars) demonstrates that metaphors must be conceivable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid metaphors and images that the reader cannot form mentally or that violate commonsense imagery. An image should be vivid and yet possible to picture; otherwise it reads as absurd rather than sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Intentionality
rubrics_metrics.description: characters act from believable motivations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether characters' actions are motivated and interpretable as rational/intentional given their traits and the plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narration and Point of View
rubrics_metrics.description: Control of narrative voice and point of view is essential; the choice (omniscient, limited, first person, etc.) must be maintained or altered with clear purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate consistency and appropriateness: does the chosen viewpoint allow necessary knowledge without authorial intrusions that break illusion? Sudden, unexplained shifts of perspective weaken authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong narrative voice / point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: A compelling or distinctive voice can establish character and context efficiently and carry the story's force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a confident, memorable voice; voice can compensate for limited scope and help the piece feel complete and singular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue should suggest life rather than slavishly reproduce speech; it must reveal character and advance the story while remaining intelligible and purposeful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge dialogue by how much it reveals indirectly—social position, education, temperament—without becoming mere exposition. Avoid transcript-like realism that burdens the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage narrative momentum and timing to sustain reader interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included with plotting and love-scene advice; pacing guidance helps maintain engagement across the novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery and metaphorical complexity versus rhetorical or prosaic expression
rubrics_metrics.description: A poem may be praised for vivid imagery and condensation, or criticized as 'prose chopped up to fit a metrical scheme' with rhetorical phrases rather than rich metaphor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the density and appropriateness of images: do they enrich thought or merely ornament it? Beware calling concentrated poetic diction 'prose' without testing how the verse shapes experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct narrative voice / point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustain a clear, specific first-person viewpoint that conveys age, temperament, and perspective (here: a child's retrospective voice that mixes immediacy with reflective commentary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use idiomatic cadence, selective vocabulary, and perspective-specific observations to make voice believable and consistent. Examples: the child's shameful, proud, and fearful registers ("I deserved it", "I forced myself to walk very slowly"). Avoid slipping into an adult omniscient narrator or flattening voice into generic description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original premise or fresh treatment of familiar premise
rubrics_metrics.description: "Original premise or fresh treatment of familiar premise" (A-range bullet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality or a novel take on a known trope helps earn A-range grades. Lack of originality can contribute to predictability or flatness noted in lower ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader competence and the use of false advance mentions (narrative snares)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can rely on readers' growing competence to detect 'seeds' and can deliberately offer false advance mentions (snares) to mislead or play with expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As readers acquire the ability to decode narrative codes, the author may include false snares; once the reader outmaneuvers these, the author may escalate to more sophisticated false snares. This is part of Proustian believability and the 'logic of inconsistency'—manipulating frustrated expectations and surprises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm and Cadence of Prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose rhythm—the musical quality produced by sentence length, punctuation, and arrangement—is a crucial aesthetic element of the novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary sentence and paragraph lengths to create momentum, repose, or emphasis. Attend to the sound and flow of language; spacing of clauses and choice of words affect the reader's emotional response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure, conflict, and momentum that drive narrative events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether plot advances logically, maintains conflict and escalation, and ties back to emotional or thematic stakes; ensure scenes contribute to movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposition-only scenes are boring: drama requires change
rubrics_metrics.description: Undramatized exposition—scenes that convey information without change—fails to create meaning regardless of mood or production values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid writing expository scenes that rely on mood to carry them; instead dramatize information through conflict, beats, and a turning point that alters value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure: From Expansive to Concise
rubrics_metrics.description: Novels often embrace complexity, exploring themes and developing settings in detail; screenplays prioritize visual storytelling over descriptive text and require distilling vast narrative content into a lean, efficient format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert paragraphs of description into concise scene headings and minimal action lines. Focus on what is necessary to convey setting and tone on screen; remove excess exposition that slows cinematic pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative and vivid description
rubrics_metrics.description: Good novel settings require imaginative and vivid description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immerse your readers in a mesmerizing fictional world so they will want to turn the page, not close the book. Use sensory detail and striking images to make places memorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: sensory description
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze sensory detail (visual, auditory, tactile, etc.) and its contribution to mood and meaning.
